findings.text: When the captured stack has fewer than three lines, `stackWithoutTwoTopLines` becomes '' and `String(err.stack).endsWith('')` is always true. The old regex left the stack unchanged in that case, so the append happened. Now the async call-site stack is silently never appended. For example, `dummy.stack` = 'at a\nat b' with an existing `err.stack` means the request-origin frames are dropped.

If the captured stack has no newline, the new code returns '' (line 17). The old `replace(/^.+\n/, '')` left a single-line stack intact. A one-frame stack such as 'at foo' now gives `err.stack = ''` when `err.stack` was empty, so that frame is lost.
